text: Rainbow Raider, whose real name is Roy G. Bivolo, is a supervillain in DC Comics. His name is a pun based on the acronym "ROYGBIV," a mnemonic for the colors of a rainbow. He is a minor, though recurring, enemy of the Flash and other heroes. Two incarnations of Rainbow Raider appear in The Flash: Roy G. Bivolo appears in the first and ninth seasons, portrayed by Paul Anthony, and a female version named Carrie Bates appears in the seventh season, portrayed by Jona Xiao. Rainbow Raider first appeared in The Flash #286 (June 1980) and was created by Cary Bates and Don Heck. In a 2008 interview, Bates stated that Rainbow Raider's color-blindness, along with his color-emotion powers and origin, was an attempt to emulate classic Rogues' Gallery villain origins he admired from the 1960s. Bates further explained that having grown up with a Flash Rogues' Gallery full of villains who weaponized elements like mirrors, cold, heat, magic, and boomerangs, Julie and he believed the color spectrum gimmick could be a worthwhile addition. As a child, Roy G. Bivolo dreamed of becoming an artist despite being completely colorblind; he painted technically skilled works that were criticized for being made of clashing colors. His father, an optometrist, tried to cure his condition and developed sophisticated goggles that produce rainbow light beams. As the Rainbow Raider, he commits crimes primarily targeting art galleries, claiming that if he cannot appreciate art due to his disability, no one else will. After being imprisoned at Belle Reve Penitentiary, he joins the Color Queens gang alongside Crazy Quilt, Doctor Light, Doctor Spectro, and Multi-Man. Roy is later killed by Blacksmith; he is temporarily resurrected as a Black Lantern during Blackest Night and permanently resurrected in The New 52 continuity reboot, where he is known as Chroma. Since his death, a team of color-themed supervillains have named themselves the Rainbow Raiders in his honor. His powers come from the goggles he wears, enabling him to project solid beams of rainbow-colored light for offensive use or as a slide for travel, and to coat people in specific colors of light to induce emotions—such as making someone sad with blue light. Heavy.com lists Rainbow Raider as one of the worst supervillains of all time, and Francesco Marciuliano from Smosh.com ranked his gadget as one of the worst supervillain gadgets of all time. Rainbow Raider also appears in Teen Titans Go! To the Movies.
